claims.text: The initial FeCoNi high-entropy alloy is single-phase FCC.
Nanostructuring FeCoNi to a grain size below 100 nm introduces grain boundaries relevant to coercivity.
Grain boundaries pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning at grain boundaries increases the coercive field of single-phase FCC FeCoNi-based alloys.
Nanostructuring will increase coercive field by a factor of 2–5 relative to single-phase FCC FeCoNi.
The coercive field of the single-phase FCC FeCoNi baseline is no greater than 100 Oe.
The proposed intervention is intended to apply only to FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 2–5-fold increase, but the falsification rule only requires a statistically significant increase. A significant increase smaller than twofold would fail the quantitative prediction while not falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
